construction.implementation_origin: Written from scratch in the designated isolated build directory; no other build or repository files were read or copied.
construction.runtime: Python 3 standard library; run with -B to avoid bytecode artifacts

input.schema_version: Integer 1; booleans are not integers in this schema.
input.synthetic: Must be true; all supplied data is explicitly synthetic.
input.documents: Array of {id: unique nonempty string, text: string}. Text can be empty.

extraction.document_ids: Unique existing document IDs in extraction precedence order.
extraction.fields: Array of {id, pattern, type, required}. Pattern is a Python regular expression with exactly one capture group; type is string, integer or boolean; required is boolean.

input.questions: Array of {id, text, required_fields}. Required fields reference extraction field IDs.
input.knowledge_base: Array of {id, question, source, requires}. Source is a document reference. Requires maps extraction field IDs to exact, type-checked scalar values.
input.actions: Array of {id, title, priority, requires_fields, requires_answers, prerequisites, research_topics}. Priority is an integer; all other references are unique string arrays. Prerequisites form an acyclic graph.
input.completed_actions: Unique action IDs whose prerequisites are also completed.
input.research_questions: Object mapping nonempty topic IDs to nonempty research question strings.
input.claims: Array of {id, topic, stance, source}. Topic references research_questions; stance is supports or opposes. These are fixture-authored annotations, not model-inferred claims.

source_reference.start: Nonnegative integer Unicode character offset, inclusive
source_reference.end: Integer Unicode character offset, exclusive; start < end <= document length

shared_schema.quoted_source: A source_reference plus text exactly equal to the source document slice.

output_envelope.status: ok for a valid execution, including abstained answers or blocked journeys
output_envelope.extract: {values, spans, missing_fields, required_missing}; every declared field has a typed value and exact quoted source or null/null.
output_envelope.faq: {answers}; every question has {id, status, answer, source, kb_id, score, reason, missing_fields}. Status is answered or abstained.
output_envelope.journey: {status, completed_actions, next_actions, steps, blocked}; status is ready, partial or blocked. Each selected step contains step, action_id, title, prerequisites and research_topics.
output_envelope.deep: {topics, synthesis, disagreements, unresolved_questions}; each synthesis includes topic, question, assessment, document_ids and cited evidence.

shared_schema.error_envelope: {status: error, error: human-readable string}; one JSON object on stdout and exit code 2.
validation: A single Validator class and shared type, reference, source and structural comparison helpers serve all four stages.
Input objects reject missing and unknown keys, duplicate IDs, unresolved references, invalid types, invalid regex captures, source bounds, cycles and inconsistent completed prerequisite sets.
The CLI also rejects duplicate JSON object keys, nonfinite numeric constants, malformed JSON and file/encoding errors.
Each stage validates the entire prior state, copies it without mutation, appends its own result, then validates the extended state.
Handoff validation recomputes bounded deterministic expectations to reject forged missing fields, ineligible or ungrounded answers, invalid journey ordering and fabricated research.
Semantic equality is recursive and type-strict, so true cannot impersonate an integer.

cross_stage_handoffs.data: Validated extracted values and missing fields
cross_stage_handoffs.effect: Missing question prerequisites cause explicit abstention; values select applicable KB policies through exact typed requirements.

cross_stage_handoffs.data: Validated answers, answer statuses and retained extraction state
cross_stage_handoffs.effect: Only answered prerequisite questions and present required fields permit actions. The plan adds its first action to simulated completion before selecting the second.

cross_stage_handoffs.data: Validated selected steps and their research topics
cross_stage_handoffs.effect: Only topics attached to actual selected steps enter evidence synthesis; blocked, unselected actions cannot add research topics.

behavior.extraction: Search selected documents in configured order, then regex matches in source order. Trim captures while preserving exact source offsets. Use the first nonempty, successfully converted match; skip invalid matches. Integer conversion accepts signed ASCII decimal digits. Boolean conversion accepts true/false/yes/no case-insensitively. Missing required fields are reported rather than causing schema failure.
behavior.retrieval: Compare question and KB-question Unicode word-token sets after casefolding and a fixed stopword filter. Use Jaccard overlap >= 0.2 among KB entries whose requirements match. Highest overlap wins, then lexical KB ID. Scores measure lexical relevance, not factual confidence.
behavior.answers: Return the selected source quote verbatim, never generated advice. Abstain with missing_required_fields or no_relevant_evidence and null answer/source. Eligibility and citations are checked at every handoff.
behavior.journey: Higher integer priority wins, then lexical action ID. next_actions lists all immediately eligible uncompleted actions. Select at most two distinct actions sequentially, rechecking monotonic prerequisites after the simulated first completion. ready means exactly two validated steps; partial means one; blocked means none. blocked records initial-state blockers and may contain an action unlocked for step two. Required fields test presence, not truthiness. Nothing is executed or marked persistently complete.
behavior.research: Group fixture-authored evidence annotations by selected research topic, preserving exact quotes and distinct source document IDs. Assess supported, opposed, disputed or insufficient_evidence. Record both sides rather than resolving conflict. Report unresolved questions for absent evidence, a single source document, conflicting evidence, or no journey topics. Assessment describes supplied evidence stances, not established real-world truth.
behavior.determinism: No randomness, timestamps, mutable global state or external calls in pipeline output. The input and prior stage states are not mutated.

included: One runnable integrated Python CLI and importable stage functions
One versioned input contract and progressively extended shared output envelope
Typed schema-driven extraction, exact source spans and missing-field reporting
Lexical KB retrieval, grounded quotations and explicit abstention
Prerequisite-aware next actions and a validated two-step or explicitly incomplete journey
Multi-document evidence synthesis with disagreement and unresolved questions
Clearly labeled synthetic fixtures and executable standard-library regression tests
excluded: LLM calls or LLM-specific steps; no injection hook is needed or used
Networks, provider SDKs, external dependencies, agents or git
PDF/OCR parsing, embedding indexes, web crawling or live data ingestion
Semantic entailment or independent verification of fixture-authored claim stances
Global optimal planning, mutually exclusive actions, or persistent action execution
Enterprise security, throughput guarantees or sandboxing of arbitrary hostile regex patterns
Production deployment, databases, authentication and user interfaces

test_outcomes.example_cli_stdout: Exactly one JSON object with status ok
coverage: All four stages and every cross-stage handoff
Exact source quotes, Unicode offsets, trimming, missing/invalid values, false and zero
FAQ relevance, tie breaking, policy eligibility and both abstention reasons
Prerequisite ordering, completed actions, cycles, blockers and partial journeys
Multidocument disagreement, agreement, single-source limits and absent evidence
Forged intermediate states, forged research, deterministic results and no mutation
Empty collections, unknown references, duplicate IDs and invalid schema types
Real CLI subprocess success, missing file and usage errors
Malformed JSON, duplicate keys, nonfinite constants, permission and decoding errors
